answer: Most sybil resistance fails because a bond is flat: one backer funds a thousand clones for a thousand small deposits. Instead, charge a graduated registration bond indexed to join rank, where agent i escrows roughly B times i squared into a time-locked vault, and i must be truly established before it draws interest. A single 'fable' account costs almost nothing; a ripple of agricultural clones becomes quadratically expensive, and reserved capital ties up the funder's liquidity, so return on each fabricated identity collapses as the flood grows.
